Alfie Dwyer, working as ze.zima, is an interdisciplinary artist creating strange kinetic objects where mechanical systems collide with fragmented images. In Secret Programs, printed fragments ,mounted onto moving PLA components, driven by a gear motor and a modified Geneva mechanism. As the mechanism turns, the image is continuously broken apart and reconstructed  becoming something between an image, a machine. #art #artist #avantgarde #niche #weird

PUMP (2007) by DAVID ADEY. David Adey transforms an ordinary football into a strange kinetic sculpture. Its surface is densely covered with drywall screws, while a hidden respirator repeatedly inflates and deflates the ball, producing a slow, mechanical rhythm. Created in 2007, Pump was later included in the 2010 California Biennial at the Orange County Museum of Art. #art #avantgarde #niche #artist #weird

Artist Casey Curran creates kinetic sculptures that combine mechanical systems with forms inspired by plants and natural structures. In this prototype, layers of delicate petals are connected so that a single mechanical action produces a rippling movement across the entire structure. Instead of every element moving independently, the motion travels through the sculpture like a wave. This type of movement is central to Curran’s practice. Using motors, wires, cranks and carefully engineered mechanisms, he creates artificial flowers and organisms that bloom, flutter and contract.  The machinery is artificial, but the movement feels strangely organic ,engineering becomes a way of imitating the rhythms of living systems. #art #artist #fashion #avantgarde #design

Japanese artist Taiki Yokote  , creates unsettling kinetic sculptures that blur the boundary between life and d**th. In Until You Become Soil, animal fur is assembled into a towering, irregular structure that continuously trembles and shifts, as though something beneath its surface were still alive. The movement comes from concealed massage devices that animate the fur of deceased animals, giving an eerie sense of renewed existence. The work originated from Yokote’s inability to discard the hair left behind by his beloved dog . #art #artist #fur #sculptureart #artistsoftiktok

Reinhard Haverkamp creates kinetic sculptures that come to life through balance, gravity, and the slightest movement. Made from simple steel lines and geometric forms, his works appear to float effortlessly, constantly shifting between stability and motion. In this piece, a gentle touch sets the sculpture into a slow, hypnotic rotation, transforming minimalist shapes into an ever-changing drawing in space. Haverkamp reveals how movement itself can become the artwork, inviting viewers to experience sculpture as a living process rather than a static object. #artist #art #avantgarde #minimalism  #niche

by Nie Shichang. Created as his 2025 graduation project at the China Academy of Art, The Cyclic Apparatus is a kinetic sculpture featuring two fish inspired by the Tai Chi yin-yang symbol. Driven by an intricate mechanical system, the figures move continuously in an endless cycle. Combining forms reminiscent of ancient Chinese bronze with contemporary engineering, Nie Shichang turns philosophical ideas of repetition, time and cosmic order into physical movement. #artist #art #avantgarde #niche #weird

Kinetic sculptor Reuben Margolin  creates intricate mechanical installations inspired by mathematics, natural movement, and wave phenomena. Cadence (2024) is a suspended sculpture measuring approximately 3.35 meters in diameter. A single electric motor controls 216 strings connected to an articulated hexagonal lattice made from tapered maple dowels. As the strings move, the wooden structure produces continuous, fluid waves, resembling the movement of water. His Caterpillar Clock (2026) explores a different form of mechanical motion. Built from polished brass, its precisely counterbalanced mechanism uses a small electric motor to move around a large gear, completing one revolution every six minutes. #art #artist #niche #sculpture #design

Artist Rachel Youn creates kinetic sculptures and installations that combine artificial plants, discarded consumer objects and mechanical devices to imitate the movements of living organisms. In Pretty Behavior (2026), Youn modifies a neck massager and connects it to an artificial orchid and leaves using metal hardware, chains and glass. Once activated, the machine makes the flower shake and move continuously, giving the synthetic plant an uncanny appearance of life. Youn frequently repurposes massagers and other machines originally designed to act on the human body, redirecting their repetitive movements into artificial plants. The objects appear to dance, struggle or react despite having no consciousness. #artist #art #niche #weird #avantgarde
